_meta.indication: EDURANT, in combination with other antiretroviral agents, is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in antiretroviral treatment-naïve adult patients.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-national, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled trial comparing TMC278 (rilpivirine) 25 mg q.d. vs efavirenz (EFV) 600 mg q.d.; in C209 the N(t)RTI background regimen was fixed to tenofovir disoproxil fumarate plus emtricitabine.
pivotal_trials.population: Antiretroviral treatment-naïve HIV-1 infected adults with plasma HIV-1 RNA ≥ 5000 copies/mL.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with plasma viral load < 50 copies/mL at Week 48 (TLOVR); non-inferiority vs EFV with a maximum allowable difference of 12%.
pivotal_trials.result: Non-inferiority of TMC278 vs EFV demonstrated in C209; TLOVR virologic response at Week 48 was 83% for both groups, 95% CI of the difference (-5.5%, 5.7%).

pivotal_trials.design: Identical in design to C209 (randomized, double-blind, active-controlled vs efavirenz), differing in that the background regimen consisted of 2 investigator-selected N(t)RTIs (tenofovir DF plus emtricitabine, or zidovudine plus lamivudine, or abacavir plus lamivudine).
pivotal_trials.population: Antiretroviral treatment-naïve HIV-1 infected adults with plasma HIV-1 RNA ≥ 5000 copies/mL.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with plasma viral load < 50 copies/mL at Week 48 (TLOVR); non-inferiority vs EFV with a maximum allowable difference of 12%.
pivotal_trials.result: Non-inferiority of TMC278 vs EFV demonstrated; TLOVR virologic response at Week 48 was 85.6% (TMC278) vs 81.7% (EFV), 95% CI of the difference (-1.6%, 9.5%).

key_safety: Most common ADRs (≥ Grade 2, ≥2% incidence) were depression, insomnia, headache and rash. In the pooled Phase 3 safety population (N=1368; EDURANT n=686), rates (EDURANT vs efavirenz) were depressive disorders 4% vs 3%, insomnia 3% vs 3%, headache 3% vs 3%, and rash 3% vs 11%. Discontinuation due to ADR was 2% (EDURANT) vs 4% (efavirenz).
target_moa: Rilpivirine is a diarylpyrimidine non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI) of HIV-1 that inhibits HIV-1 replication by non-competitive inhibition of HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT); it does not inhibit human cellular DNA polymerases α, β and γ.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; this application was not presented before the Antiviral Products Advisory Committee because it was the fifth NNRTI in the class with a comparable adverse event profile.

basis.text: The NDA received a standard (not priority) 10-month review because it was the fifth NNRTI in the class with a comparable adverse event profile.

citations.quote: This NDA was submitted on July 23, 2010 and received a standard 10-month review because it was the fifth NNRTI in the class with a comparable adverse event profile. For similar reasons, this application was not presented before the Antiviral Products Advisory Committee.

summary.text: This NDA, submitted and received July 23, 2010, received a standard 10-month review (not priority, accelerated, or breakthrough) because rilpivirine was the fifth NNRTI in its class with a comparable adverse event profile, and the application was not presented to an advisory committee. Approval was based on Week 48 non-inferiority efficacy versus efavirenz in two Phase 3 treatment-naïve trials (ECHO and THRIVE).

citations.quote: This NDA was submitted on July 23, 2010 and received a standard 10-month review because it was the fifth NNRTI in the class with a comparable adverse event profile. For similar reasons, this application was not presented before the Antiviral Products Advisory Committee.

The evidence of efficacy of EDURANT is based on the analyses of 48-week data from 2 randomized, double-blinded, active controlled, Phase 3 trials TMC278-C209 (ECHO) and TMC278-C215 (THRIVE) and from a 96-week (with extension to 192 weeks) randomized, active-controlled, dose-comparison Phase 2b trial in antiretroviral treatment-naïve adults.

requirement.text: 1768-4: Conduct a clinical trial in healthy subjects to evaluate the effect of rilpivirine at steady state on the single-dose pharmacokinetics of digoxin.

citations.quote: 1768-4 Conduct a clinical trial in healthy subjects to evaluate the effect of rilpivirine at steady state on the single dose pharmacokinetics of digoxin. The pharmacokinetics of digoxin when coadministered with rilpivirine (test arm) will be compared to the pharmacokinetics of digoxin by itself (reference arm). The primary digoxin pharmacokinetic parameters that will be evaluated are AUC(0→∞), AUC(0→t), and Cmax.
